newsitem.title: FRANCE: IHT mulls moving some operations from Paris.
newsitem.headline: IHT mulls moving some operations from Paris.

text.p: The International Herald Tribune, published in Paris since 1887, is considering moving part of its operations out of France to bring down costs, executives said on Tuesday.
"A feasibility study is under way. It's a matter of whether or not portions of the paper could be done elsewhere more cost-effectively," executive editor Michael Getler said.

Officials said recommendations were expected in March or April. Even if a move was decided, only some operations -- most likely editing functions -- would be moved out of Paris, either to New York, Washington or perhaps Asia, officials said.

"It's absolutely not imminent and probably not even likely," Getler told Reuters. "But given the high cost of operating in France, it certainly is a good thing to do...to look into the cost of moving parts of the newspaper elsewhere".
"In any case, the Tribune is certainly going to remain in Paris. A large news and editorial presence would remain here," he said.

The newspaper, which is published Monday through Saturday and is co-owned by the New York Times and Washington Post companies, "is in the situation that all daily papers are in these days. We need to reduce the cost base," Herald Tribune spokesman Bruce Singer said.
The study is being undertaken by the Times with the Post's support, officials said. The Times has been under pressure from major shareholders to perform better financially.
Editorial employees who pleaded anonymity said management seemed particularly concerned about the high cost of health and holiday benefits in France.
The newspaper has about 250 employees in Paris, including some 50 (corrects number) editorial workers.
It "lost a bit of money last year but is doing very well this year," Singer said, with advertising sales on the rise and circulation up 1.5 percent since 1994 to 192,000.
The newspaper is printed at 12 different sites around the world including New York, five plants in Europe and three in Asia. A 13th site is to be announced soon, Springer said.
The newspaper started its life as an offshoot of the New York Herald. The Paris edition continued after the American paper shut down in 1966.
